entry.name: Binh Thi Nguyen Slavicka
entry.department: Institute of Asian Studies, Faculty of Arts

evidence.currentRole: https://uas.ff.cuni.cz/ustav/profily-akademiku/binh-slavicka/ — current institutional academic profile for Ing. Binh Slavická, Ph.D.; employment since 1992 at the Institute of Far Eastern Studies / Institute of Asian Studies and current Vietnamese-language courses. https://vietnam.ff.cuni.cz/o-nas/lide/ separates three internal teachers (including Slavická) from external instructors. Full-time continuing teaching is corroborated by her first-person interview at https://www.asiaskop.cz/asie-cr/lidska-hloupost-je-vsude-stejna-svejka-si-ve-vietnamu-pochvaluji-rika-prekladatelka-binh-slavicka : “V roce 1992 jsem nastoupila na plný úvazek” (joined full-time in 1992). Current staff directory also opened: https://is.cuni.cz/webapps/whois2/osoba/1058204373463705/?lang=en . Teaching track reflects the documented continuing internal teaching appointment; no tenure claim is made.
evidence.doctorateOrPapers: https://uas.ff.cuni.cz/ustav/profily-akademiku/binh-slavicka/ — Ph.D. in the title; doctoral studies at FF UK (Charles University Faculty of Arts), 2008–2016, dissertation on particles in modern Vietnamese. Degree year omitted because the opened profile gives a study range rather than an explicit award date.
evidence.vietnameseSignal: Vietnamese given name Binh; the opened first-person Asiaskop interview states schooling in Vietnam and selection for study in Czechoslovakia. Charles University book announcement https://iforum.cuni.cz/IFORUM-5832-version1.pdf explicitly identifies the author as Slavická, Nguyen Thi Binh. Its title, book, publisher and ISBN match the book on her employer profile. PDF was retrieved live by Python urllib (HTTP 200, application/pdf) and read through pdftotext in memory after web.open returned a cache miss. Canonical name places Binh first and retains original surname Nguyen before married surname Slavicka, with diacritics removed. No reconstructed vietnameseName.
evidence.dedup: Ran npm run find-roster-matches -- "Binh Slavicka" --url https://uas.ff.cuni.cz/ustav/profily-akademiku/binh-slavicka/ https://vietnam.ff.cuni.cz/o-nas/lide/binh-slavicka/ : no roster or retired-id matches. Reran with "Binh Thi Nguyen Slavicka" and the WhoIS URL: name-only hits vp-0476 C. Thi Nguyen (Utah philosophy, UCLA PhD 2011), vp-1528 Binh P. Nguyen (Wellington data science, NUS PhD 2014), vp-3148 Binh Nguyen (EntoZyme insect biology, Macquarie PhD 2021). All are different people by field, degree and identity URLs. Manual normalized-name check found no Slavicka or Charles University Binh entry. Not in already-proposed.txt.
evidence.enrichment: Department, research areas and doctorate institution are supported by the academic profile; Prague/Czech Republic by the current university WhoIS address. The university announcement https://www.ff.cuni.cz/2022/10/dr-binh-slavicka-ziskala-cenu-gratias-agit-2022/ confirms her leadership of Vietnamese studies and Gratias agit 2022 recognition. That recognition concerns international cultural relations and is omitted from honors under the roster exclusion for community-engagement awards. No verified Google Scholar, LinkedIn or separate personal/lab homepage found. Portrait not proposed: the academic profile has no clearly verified individual headshot, and the award-news image was not visually vetted. No image downloaded.

Broad regional searches covered Slovakia, Slovenia, Croatia, Greece, Romania, Bulgaria, Serbia, the Baltic states, Malta, Cyprus, Russia and Ukraine. No additional employer-verified eligible university appointment found. These were search-level reconnaissance, not complete institutional-directory sweeps. Ireland/New Zealand, DACH, Nordic/Benelux and Turkey were excluded after consulting slices.tsv because separate slices cover them. Non-university institutes were excluded. All-field searches included academic ranks in English/Italian/Spanish/Polish/Czech plus Vietnamese names and university affiliation; strongest actual employer-page coverage was CS/engineering, business/economics and humanities. This is a bounded discovery pass, not an assertion of exhaustive coverage of every European university. Stopped after repeated searches returned existing entries or excluded/unsupported appointments rather than padding the 25-candidate maximum.
